description:
FILED s543k (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-23) from the reviewing session's k-09 probe list of s543k member 4 (#5255): the siblings of `delete $h{fh};` that DROP an escaped output handle in a container.  PRE-EXISTING: base 4a0fd0ec the same; wrong at FILE LEVEL too, so outside the eval edge (#5255 took the eval half of the shapes s543g flushes: `undef $x` / `$x = undef` / a void `delete`).

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 prints 5 on each | PCL 0):
    my $f = "/tmp/x.$$"; my %h; { open my $t, ">", $f or die; print $t "hdata"; $h{fh} = $t; } %h = (); print -s $f, "\n";
  and the same with `%h = ();` replaced by `$h{fh} = undef;` / `undef %h;`; with an ARRAY holder
    my $f = "/tmp/x.$$"; my @a; { open my $t, ">", $f or die; print $t "hdata"; $a[0] = $t; } $a[0] = undef; print -s $f, "\n";
  and `$a[0] = undef;` replaced by `splice(@a, 0, 1);` / `pop @a;`; and the TAIL of a file-level sub (s543g's wrap asks for a `:void` statement; a sub's last statement is `inherit`):
    ... sub drop { delete $h{fh} } drop(); print -s $f, "\n";     # perl 5 | PCL 0
(probe files: s543k scratch/s543k/p4b/probes.txt k10t..k15t, p4b/subtail.pl.)

WHAT IT IS: the drop flush (ir-spec 6.5b) runs at `undef $x;` / `$x = undef;` (Parser2::_fh_drop_flush_var), at a void `delete ELEM;` (Pl::Stmt::drop_delete_shape -> p-flush-dropped-value) and, since s543g, one level inside the dropped value; a container CLEARED or SHRUNK by an assignment, `undef %h`, `splice` or `pop`, and an element overwritten with undef, drop the handle without passing any of them.  Same family as #5254 (the package-variable half).  FIX DIRECTION (not designed): the statement classifier's drop shapes (Pl::Stmt) gain these spellings and the flush reads the OLD value(s) before the store, bounded like %p-flush-dropped-value (+p-flush-walk-limit+); the sub-tail case is the void wrap taking `inherit` where a flush is invisible (it returns the value) -- measure the emission it moves (every sub ending in `delete $self->{k}`).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a container cleared or shrunk (`%h = ()`, `undef %h`, `$h{fh} = undef`, `$a[0] = undef`, `splice`, `pop`) or a sub-tail `delete $h{fh}` drops an escaped output handle without writing it out -- the drop flush covers `undef $x` / a void `delete` only
triage_reason: a silent wrong of when bytes reach a file (an escaped handle in a container): IN, LOW-MEDIUM (the #5254 / ns-escaping-filehandle family)
